We had been registered with Yorkshire vets for many years for various pets but at the birkenshaw surgery. Fortunately we hadn’t had the need to visit for around 5 years until our dog suddenly fell ill a few months ago. No appointments were available at birkenshaw so we had to visit the Morley branch.
We were instantly met with worst case senarios and extortionate prices for things that may or may not help. We left feeling completely disheartened and told to bring her back the next day. Fortunately we saw a different vet the next day who was far more positive and didn’t agree with the previous possible diagnosis but did mention another potentially fatal diagnosis. More money was spent for more drugs and off we went to see how she went. After picking up briefly she then deteriorated again and this time we managed to be seen at the birkenshaw surgery we decided to have blood and urine tests done there and then… then I received a call from the first vet who again suggested an ultrasound for between £1200-850 depending on where and when they would “fit us in” … it could be this it could be that but their suggestion was funnily enough to have the ultra sound done regardless and then maybe more bloods and basically go back to square one and pay for it all again. After loosing complete faith and seeing no light at the end of the tunnel we decided to get a second opinion. Took her to Calder vets that evening -£150 FAST scan diagnosed the issue and emergency surgery was booked for the next morning. Our beloved Lottie had the best care there and is now like a puppy again. I’d never use Yorkshire vets ever again. Money money money seems to be their main concern. We spent around £800 for absolutely nothing there.
Very friendly and helpful staff very clean environment. Everything was explained properly about my pet would recommend this practice.
Always friendly and professional. Clean and tidy environment and always on time.
Excellent service as always

I would strongly encourage pet owners to carefully consider whether this practice is the right choice for their beloved animals.

I was a client of this practice for over ten years. However, following the change in ownership, I experienced not only significant increases in pricing but, more concerningly, what I believe was a noticeable decline in the standard of care my cats received.

In my experience, this decline ultimately resulted in the avoidable loss of one of my cats. Over the course of more than a year, his condition was, in my view, not managed appropriately, and he did not receive the dignified, pain-free end-of-life care that every pet deserves. This was an incredibly distressing experience that has had a lasting impact on me.

I also encountered repeated issues with basic standards of care. On several occasions, after collecting my cats following procedures, they were returned to me covered in faeces. This is not a standard of care that I consider acceptable.

More recently, after transferring to another veterinary practice, I discovered that a diagnosis previously given to one of my cats was incorrect. I had received a phone call informing me that he had aggressive, malignant cancer, news that completely turned my life upside down. After further investigations elsewhere, I have been informed that he does not have cancer. The emotional distress caused by receiving such a serious and ultimately inaccurate diagnosis is difficult to put into words.

In my opinion, these experiences reflect serious shortcomings in the care provided. While I have always found the reception staff to be kind, courteous, and compassionate, their professionalism cannot compensate for what I believe to be significant failings in the veterinary care my pets received.

Based on my personal experience, I cannot recommend this practice and would urge others to consider their options carefully before entrusting their pets to its care.

Yorkshire Vets is owned by IVC, a private equity backed company whose sole objective is to bleed pet owners dry.

The staff and vets are lovely but their parent company is making them charge £200 a month for two generic drugs that are available online for £15.  It is unprincipled and immoral.

If you ask for the prescription only service (so that you can get the drugs online) they will charge you £35 per prescription. My lovely pooch with a heart condition which is routine for his age could be treated for £15 a month. He is being charged £200 a month.  It is nothing less than extortion.

Thankfully there is legislation coming in to stop this abhorrent practice but it is not coming in until September 2026. I note that until the legislation comes into force Yorkshire Vets are maxing their charges.  No early adoption of the rules for IVC. Until the legislation comes in to force - steer well clear of all private equity backed vets!! It is quite literally a disgrace.

I have moved to another veterinary practice today with no problem. After 28 years with this practice I somehow expected them to be caring and decent and reasonable as they always used to be. But the new private equity owners are finance guys.  They don’t care about pets or their owners.

Very caring people here. Flat off road car park to flat entrance. Not 24 hours at this site. Is on the corner of junction A650 so traffic can have problems turning in and out of site.  24 cover is provided by Yorkshire Vets at Thornbury  on A647 between Dawsons Corner roundabout and Dick Lane roundabout, on left going towards Bradford with steep camber down off the carriageway.

Nice welcome when we walked in.  Consultant obviously loved her job and knew what she was talking about. Very friendly and did a thorough check on Bruno and given the all clear. I felt I could trust the consultant and not be handed unneccesary medications. Bruno my dog lab retreiver who is now 10 years old stood nicely for the vet and then wanted his treat. I was told he is in good health for his age.

I cannot thank Yorkshire Vets Morley for their kindness and dedication to making the visit really special. You all have looked after Bruno since he was young. Thankyou.

Keep up the good work everyone. X

They are great, a little pricey, but I’m willing to pay for the location and how good they are with my cats. Reception staff, especially Sam, they are so friendly and reassuring especially if you are worried about something. There have been times where I have called them a few times a day due to being worried about my cats whilst in surgery, and they are so patient and reassuring, the reception staff even arranged for a nurse to call me back to speak with me about my cats (they were going in for neutering, and I have Persians) You can tell they really love animals and I feel my pets are in good hands with them. As with other vets the prices keep increasing and it is costly, so I may review whether they’re still suitable for us if this continues but for now they are great!

I've been to see two different vets on two separate occasions and both times have been poor experiences. I asked the second vet to look at my cats eye as she was having issues and the vet refused. After asking her a few times she laughed at me and suggested she could refer me to an ophthalmologist! My previous vets were fantastic and I only changed vets due to the distance. Checking an animals eyes, teeth and body should be part of every consultation but neither vet did this here.  At my last vets, when my cat had an issue with her eyes in the past they thoroughly checked it, put dye in her eye and carried out a full inspection and even took photos to send to an animal ophthalmologist to check and then updated me with their response as standard and at no extra cost. I have now moved vets as I wouldn't trust any of them at Yorkshire Vets with my cats care. The receptionists are nice though.
